en: 9. Dhammayamaka 9.2 Pavattivāra 9.2.1.
Uppādavāra (The Chapter on Arising)
9.2.1.1. Chapter on the Present (Paccuppannavāra) 9.2.1.1.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) In whom wholesome states arise, in that person do unwholesome states arise? No.
Or again, when unwholesome states arise in someone, do wholesome states arise in that person? No.
When wholesome states arise in someone, do indeterminate states arise in that person?
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states in the formless realm, wholesome states arise for them, but indeterminate states do not.
Dhammas arise. At the moment of the arising of wholesome states in the five-aggregate plane, both wholesome dhammas and indeterminate dhammas arise for them.
Or else, for whomsoever indeterminate dhammas arise, do wholesome dhammas arise for them?
For all those being reborn, and at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence,
indeterminate states arise, but wholesome states do not arise for them. In the five-aggregate realm, at the moment of the arising of wholesome states,
both indeterminate states and wholesome states arise for them.
For whom unwholesome states arise, for them indeterminate states also arise?
At the moment of the arising of unwholesome states in the formless realm, unwholesome states arise for them, but indeterminate states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of unwholesome states in the fivefold plane, both unwholesome states and [indeterminate] states arise for them.
And indeterminate states arise.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states arise, do unwholesome states arise for them?
For all those being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, indeterminate [states] arise for them.

Indeterminate states arise, but unwholesome states do not arise for them. In the five-aggregate plane, at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states arise for them.
9.2.1.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states arise, do unwholesome states arise there? Yes.
Or, wherever unwholesome states arise, do wholesome states arise there? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states arise, do indeterminate states arise there? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate states arise, do wholesome states arise there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states arise there, but wholesome states do not arise there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, both indeterminate states and wholesome states arise there.
Where unwholesome states arise, do indeterminate states arise there? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate states arise, do unwholesome states also arise there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states arise there, but unwholesome states do not arise there. In the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states arise.
9.2.1.1.3. Positive Person-Space Analysis.
When wholesome states arise for someone in a certain place, do unwholesome states arise for that person in that same place? No.
Or again, when unwholesome states arise for someone in a certain place, do wholesome states arise for that person in that same place? No.
When wholesome states arise for someone in a certain place, do indeterminate states arise for that person in that same place?
In the immaterial plane, at the moment of the arising of wholesome states, wholesome phenomena arise for those [beings] there,
but indeterminate phenomena do not arise for them there. In the five-aggregate plane, at the moment of the arising of wholesome states,
both wholesome phenomena and indeterminate phenomena arise for them there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states arise at a certain place, do wholesome states also arise for them there?

For all those being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome—at these times, indeterminate states arise for them there, but wholesome states do not arise for them there. This applies to the fivefold plane.
At the moment of arising of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states arise therein.
For whomsoever unwholesome states arise therein, do indeterminate states arise for them therein?
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states in the immaterial realm, unwholesome states arise for them therein, but indeterminate states do not [arise] for them.
Therein, indeterminate states arise. In the five-aggregate plane, at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, both unwholesome states and indeterminate states arise therein.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states arise in a certain place, do unwholesome states arise for them there?
For all those being reborn, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from unwholesome states,

indeterminate phenomena arise there, but unwholesome phenomena do not arise there for them. For those in the five-aggregate realm at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate phenomena and unwholesome phenomena arise there.
9.2.1.1.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not arise, for that person do unwholesome states not arise?
At the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, for those [persons] wholesome states do not arise, but unwholesome states do arise.
They do not arise. For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness,
for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from both the wholesome and the unwholesome, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings—
neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states arise for them.
Or again, for whom unwholesome states do not arise, for them do wholesome states not arise?
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, unwholesome states do not arise for them, but wholesome states do not fail to arise for them.
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those whose consciousness is dissociated from the unwholesome and dissociated from the wholesome...
At the moment of arising, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings,
neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states arise.
For one in whom wholesome states do not arise, do indeterminate states not arise?
For all those being reborn, and for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence, wholesome states do not arise;

yet it is not that indeterminate states do not arise for them. For all those passing away, for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and for those at the moment of the arising of unwholesome consciousness in the formless realm, both wholesome states and... [indeterminate states do not arise].
Indeterminate states do not arise. Or, for whom indeterminate states do not arise, do wholesome states not arise for them?

In the immaterial plane, at the moment of the arising of wholesome states, for those [beings] indeterminate states do not arise, but wholesome states [do arise]. For those [beings], wholesome states do not arise.

Dhammas do not arise. For all those passing away, for one in the process of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those in the immaterial plane at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states—unfor these, neither indeterminate dhammas nor wholesome dhammas arise.
For whom unwholesome dhammas do not arise, do indeterminate dhammas not arise for them?
For all those being reborn, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from unwholesome states, unwholesome phenomena do not arise;
yet it is not that indeterminate phenomena do not arise for them.

For all those passing away, for those during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both unwholesome phenomena...
Do indeterminate states not arise? [Yes,] indeterminate states do not arise.
Or, for whom indeterminate states do not arise, do unwholesome states not arise for them?
In the immaterial plane, at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, for those [beings] indeterminate states do not arise, but unwholesome states [do] not [not arise].

Dhammas do not arise. For all those passing away, for one in the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of wholesome dhammas, neither indeterminate dhammas nor unwholesome dhammas arise.
9.2.1.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where wholesome states do not arise, there unwholesome states do not arise? Yes.
Or, where unwholesome states do not arise, there wholesome states do not arise? Yes.
Where wholesome states do not arise, there indeterminate states do not arise? They do arise.
Or, where indeterminate states do not arise, do wholesome states not arise there? There is no such case.
Where unwholesome states do not arise, do indeterminate states not arise there? They do arise.
Or, where indeterminate states do not arise, do unwholesome states not arise there? There is no such case.
9.2.1.1.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [mental] state, wholesome states do not arise, in that person and in that state do unwholesome states not arise?
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, in those persons and in that state, wholesome states do not arise; but it is not the case that unwholesome states do not arise in them in that state.
Unwholesome states do not arise. For all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness,
for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from both the wholesome and the unwholesome, and for non-percipient beings— wholesome states do not arise there,
and unwholesome states also do not arise.
Or again, for whomsoever unwholesome states do not arise at a certain place, do wholesome states not arise for them at that place?
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, unwholesome states do not arise for them there, but it is not the case that wholesome states do not arise for them there.
[This is true] for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those whose consciousness is dissociated from both the unwholesome and the wholesome.
At the moment of arising, for non-percipient beings, neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states arise there.
For one in whom wholesome states do not arise at a certain place, do indeterminate states not arise there for them?

For all those being reborn, and at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence, wholesome states do not arise therein; yet it is not that indeterminate states do not arise therein for them.

For all those passing away, at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of arising of unwholesome consciousness in the formless realm, [wholesome states do not arise therein].
Wholesome states do not arise, and indeterminate states also do not arise. Or conversely:
for whomsoever, wherever indeterminate states do not arise, for that person there wholesome states do not arise?

In the immaterial plane, at the moment of the arising of wholesome states, for those [beings] indeterminate states do not arise there, yet it is not the case that for those [beings] wholesome states do not arise.
In that case, wholesome states do not arise. For all those passing away, for one during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness,
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states— neither indeterminate states nor wholesome states arise therein.
For whom, where unwholesome states do not arise, for them there do not arise indeterminate states?

For all those being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome—for them, there unwholesome states do not arise, but it is not that indeterminate states do not arise for them there. For all...
For those at the moment of death, during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of wholesome states—
do unwholesome states not arise and indeterminate states also not arise therein?
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states do not arise therein, do unwholesome states also not arise therein?
In the immaterial realm (arūpa), at the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, indeterminate states do not arise for them there, but unwholesome states do not fail to arise for them there.
For all those passing away, during the subsistence of consciousness, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness in the immaterial realm,
and at the moment of the arising of wholesome states in the immaterial realm, neither indeterminate nor unwholesome states arise for them there.
And these phenomena do not arise.
9.2.1.2. Chapter on the Past (Atītavāra) 9.2.1.2.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala)
For whomsoever wholesome states had arisen, for that person unwholesome states had arisen? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states had arisen, for that person wholesome states had arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states had arisen, for that person indeterminate states had arisen? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states had arisen, had wholesome states arisen for them? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states had arisen, had indeterminate states arisen for them? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states had arisen, had unwholesome states arisen for them? Yes.
9.2.1.2.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa) Wherever wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) had arisen, there unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) had also arisen? Yes.
Or, wherever unwholesome states had arisen, there wholesome states had also arisen? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states (*kusala-dhamma*) had arisen, there had indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) arisen? Yes.
Or, wherever indeterminate states had arisen, there had wholesome states arisen?

In the case of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), indeterminate states had arisen there, but wholesome states had not arisen there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence (*catuvokāra* and *pañcavokāra*), both indeterminate states and wholesome states had arisen there.
Where unwholesome states had arisen, there had unwholesome states arisen? Yes.
Or else, where indeterminate states had arisen, there had unwholesome states arisen?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states had arisen there, but unwholesome states had not arisen there. In the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states had arisen there.
9.2.1.2.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) In whomsoever unwholesome states had arisen at a certain place, had wholesome states also arisen for that person at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, in whomsoever unwholesome states had arisen at a certain place, had wholesome states also arisen for that person at that same place? Yes.
When a second unwholesome consciousness is occurring in the Pure Abodes, unwholesome states have arisen therein for them,
but wholesome states have not arisen therein for them. For others— those belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes—
both unwholesome states and wholesome states have arisen therein.
For whomsoever wholesome states had arisen at a certain place, for that person at that place had indeterminate states arisen? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states had arisen at a certain place, for that person at that place had wholesome states arisen?
For those in the second moment of consciousness of the Pure Abodes, and for non-percipient beings—at those places, indeterminate states [had arisen].
[In the case of] those four-aggregate or five-aggregate beings, indeterminate states had arisen there, but wholesome states had not arisen for them there.
For others—those four-aggregate or five-aggregate beings—both indeterminate states and wholesome states had arisen there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states had arisen at a certain place, had indeterminate states also arisen for them at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely: For whomsoever indeterminate (abyākata) states had arisen at a certain place, had unwholesome (akusala) states also arisen for them at that same place?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), and for those non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states had arisen there, but unwholesome states had not arisen for them there. For others, namely those belonging to the four-aggregate realm (catuvokāra)...
For those belonging to the five-aggregate realm, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states had arisen therein. 9.2.1.2.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states had not arisen, had unwholesome states not arisen for them? None.
Or, for whom unwholesome states did not arise, did wholesome states not arise for them? None.
For whom wholesome states did not arise, did indeterminate states not arise for them? None.
Or, for whom indeterminate states did not arise, did wholesome states not arise for them? None.
For whom unwholesome states did not arise, for them indeterminate states did not arise? None.
Or else, for whom indeterminate states did not arise, for them unwholesome states did not arise? None.
9.2.1.2.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa).
Where wholesome states had not arisen, had unwholesome states not arisen there? Yes.
Or else, where unwholesome states had not arisen, had wholesome states not arisen there? Yes.
Where wholesome states had not arisen, had indeterminate states not arisen there? They had arisen.
Or, where indeterminate states (abyākata-dhammā) had not arisen, had wholesome states (kusala-dhammā) not arisen there? None.
Where unwholesome states (akusala-dhammā) had not arisen, had indeterminate states not arisen there? They had arisen.
Or, where indeterminate states had not arisen, had unwholesome states not arisen there? None.
9.2.1.2.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom and in what [sphere] wholesome states had not arisen, for them and in that [sphere] unwholesome states had not arisen?
For those in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), while a second unwholesome consciousness was occurring, wholesome states had not arisen in them there.

And yet, unwholesome states did not arise for them there. For those Pure-Abode beings when their second consciousness was occurring, and for those non-percipient beings, neither wholesome nor unwholesome states arose there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever unwholesome states did not arise there, for that person did wholesome states not arise there? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states had not arisen at a certain place, had indeterminate states also not arisen for them at that same place?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), wholesome states had not arisen at that place, but it is not the case that indeterminate states had not arisen for them there. [This is so] for those being reborn into the Pure Abodes.
For those [beings], in that [place], both wholesome states and indeterminate states did not arise.
Or rather: for whomsoever, in whatever place, indeterminate states did not arise, for that person, in that place, did wholesome states not arise? Yes.
For whomsoever, in whatever place, unwholesome states did not arise, for that person, in that place, did indeterminate states not arise?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, unwholesome states have not arisen for those non-percipient beings there,
but indeterminate states have not failed to arise for them there. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes,
neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states have arisen there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) had not arisen at a certain place, had unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) not arisen for them there? Yes.
9.2.1.3. Future Chapter (Anāgatavāra) 9.2.1.3.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala)
Will unwholesome states arise for one in whom wholesome states will arise?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, wholesome states will arise, but unwholesome states will not arise for them.
For others, both wholesome states and unwholesome states will arise.
Unwholesome states will arise.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states will arise, will wholesome states arise for them? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states will arise, will indeterminate states arise for them? Yes.
Or again, for whom indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will arise, will wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) also arise for them?
For those who possess the supreme path (agga-magga-samaṅgī) and for Arahants, indeterminate states will arise, but wholesome states will not arise for them.
For others, both indeterminate states and wholesome states will arise.
And unwholesome states will arise.
For whom unwholesome states will arise, for that person will indeterminate states arise? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will arise, for that person will unwholesome states arise?
For those who possess the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for the Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately follows which they will attain the highest path—
unspecified (abyākata) phenomena will arise, but unwholesome (akusala) phenomena will not arise for them. For others,
both unspecified phenomena and unwholesome phenomena will arise.
9.2.1.3.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa) Where wholesome states will arise, will unwholesome states also arise there? Yes.
Or else, where unwholesome states will arise, will wholesome states also arise there? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states will arise, will indeterminate states also arise there? Yes.
Or, wherever indeterminate states will arise, will wholesome states also arise there?
In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will arise there, but wholesome states will not arise there.
In the fourfold plane and the fivefold plane, there both indeterminate states and wholesome states will arise.
Where unwholesome states will arise, will indeterminate states also arise there? Yes.
Or conversely, where indeterminate states will arise, will unwholesome states also arise there?
In the case of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), indeterminate (*abyākata*) phenomena will arise there, but unwholesome (*akusala*) phenomena will not arise there.
In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence (*vokāra*), both indeterminate phenomena and unwholesome phenomena will arise there.
9.2.1.3.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane (*Anulomapuggalokāsa*).
For whom, and in what [sphere], will wholesome states arise, for them, and in that same [sphere], will unwholesome states arise?
For those who will attain the highest path immediately after this consciousness, wholesome states will arise there, but unwholesome states will not arise there for them.
For others—namely, those belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—[both may arise].
In those [persons], both wholesome states and unwholesome states will arise therein. Or rather:
for whomsoever unwholesome states will arise in a certain place, will wholesome states also arise for that person in that same place? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states will arise in a certain place, will indeterminate states also arise for that person in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) will arise at a certain place, will wholesome states (*kusala-dhamma*) also arise for them there?

For those possessing the supreme path (*agga-maggasamaṅgī*), for Arahants, and for non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), indeterminate states will arise there, but wholesome states will not arise for them there.
For others—namely, those of the four-constituent (*catuvokāra*) and five-constituent (*pañcavokāra*) realms—[both will arise].
In those [beings], there will arise both indeterminate states and wholesome states.
For whomsoever unwholesome states will arise in a certain place, will indeterminate states also arise for them in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will arise in a certain place, will unwholesome states also arise for them in that same place?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamagga-samaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path,
and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta)— for these, indeterminate (abyākata) phenomena will arise there, but unwholesome (akusala) phenomena will not arise there.
For others— those belonging to the fourfold and fivefold aggregates— for them, indeterminate phenomena [will arise there].
...and unwholesome states will arise.
9.2.1.3.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom wholesome states will not arise, for that person will unwholesome states not arise? Yes, they will.
Or conversely, for whom unwholesome states will not arise, will wholesome states not arise for them?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, unwholesome states will not arise, but it is not the case that wholesome states will not arise for them.
For those possessing the supreme path and for Arahants, [both will not arise].
Unwholesome states will not arise, and wholesome states will not arise.
For one for whom wholesome states will not arise, will indeterminate states not arise?
For those possessing the highest path and for Arahants, wholesome states will not arise; yet for them, [indeterminate states do arise].
Indeterminate states will not arise. For those possessing the final consciousness, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise, will wholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
For whom unwholesome states will not arise, for them indeterminate states will not arise?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) and for Arahants— for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path—
unwholesome states will not arise, but it is not the case that indeterminate states will not arise for them.
For those possessing the final consciousness, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise, will unwholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
9.2.1.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states will not arise, will there unwholesome states not arise? Yes.
Or, wherever unwholesome states will not arise, will there wholesome states not arise? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states will not arise, will there indeterminate states not arise? They will arise.
Or, where indeterminate states will not arise, will there wholesome states not arise? No.
Where unwholesome states will not arise, will there indeterminate states not arise? They will arise.
Or, where indeterminate states will not arise, will there unwholesome states not arise? No.
9.2.1.3.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa) For whomsoever wholesome states will not arise in a certain place, for that person in that place, will unwholesome states not arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states will not arise in a certain place, for that person in that place, will wholesome states not arise? Yes.
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, unwholesome states will not arise therein,
but it is not the case that wholesome states will not arise therein for them. For those possessing the supreme path,
for Arahants, and for non-percipient beings, neither unwholesome nor wholesome states will arise therein.
And [it is not the case that] unwholesome states will not arise.
For whomsoever wholesome states will not arise in a certain place, will indeterminate states also not arise for them in that same place?
For those possessing the highest path (agga-magga), for Arahants, and for non-percipient beings—wholesome states will not arise for them in that place.
And yet, indeterminate states will not fail to arise there for them. For those possessing the final consciousness, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise there.
Or rather: for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise in a certain place, will wholesome states also not arise there for that person? Yes, they will.
For whom and in what [sphere] unwholesome states will not arise, for them and in that [sphere] will indeterminate states not arise?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path,
and for non-percipient beings— for these, unwholesome states will not arise there, but indeterminate states will not [necessarily] arise for them there either.
Unwholesome states will not arise. For those possessing their final consciousness, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise therein. Or conversely:
for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise therein, will unwholesome states also not arise therein for them? Yes.
9.2.1.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past (Paccuppannātītavāra) 9.2.1.4.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) In one for whom wholesome states arise, have unwholesome states arisen? Yes.
Or again, for those in whom unwholesome states have arisen, do wholesome states arise?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— unwholesome states have arisen for them, but wholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, unwholesome states have arisen and wholesome states are arising for those [persons].
For whom wholesome states are arising, have indeterminate states arisen for them? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom indeterminate states have arisen, are wholesome states arising for them?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) have arisen,
but wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) do not arise for them. At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states arise for them.
For whom unwholesome states arise, for that person have indeterminate states arisen? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom indeterminate states have arisen, for that person do unwholesome states arise?

[They do not] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome at the moment of its arising, and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation.
For those non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have arisen, but unwholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states have arisen for them.
9.2.1.4.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states arise, have unwholesome states arisen there?
… [as before] … 9.2.1.4.3. Positive Person-Space:
For whomsoever, wherever, wholesome states arise, have unwholesome states arisen for that person there? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states had arisen at a certain place, do wholesome states arise for them at that same place?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those whose consciousness is dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its arising, unwholesome states had arisen for them at that place, but wholesome states do not arise for them there. Of the wholesome...
At the moment of arising, unwholesome states had arisen and wholesome states are arising for those [persons] therein.
For whomsoever wholesome states are arising therein, had indeterminate states arisen for them therein? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states had arisen therein, are wholesome states arising for them therein?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and in non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have arisen there, but wholesome states do not arise there for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome [consciousness], for them both indeterminate states and wholesome states arise there.
For whom and in what [state] unwholesome states arise, for that person and in that state do indeterminate states also arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom and in what [state] indeterminate states have arisen, for that person and in that state do unwholesome states arise?

[They do not arise] in all [persons] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and in the case of non-percipient beings.
For them, indeterminate states had arisen there, but unwholesome states do not arise there for them.
At the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states have arisen and are arising there for them.
9.2.1.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom wholesome states do not arise, for that person have unwholesome states not arisen? They have arisen.
Or rather, for whom unwholesome states have not arisen, for that person do wholesome states not arise? There is none.
For whom wholesome states do not arise, for that person have indeterminate states not arisen? They have arisen.
Or, for whom indeterminate states (abyākatā dhammā) had not arisen, do wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) not arise for them? None.
For whom unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) do not arise, had indeterminate states not arisen for them? They had arisen.
Or, for whom indeterminate states had not arisen, do unwholesome states not arise for them? None.
9.2.1.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where wholesome states do not arise, did unwholesome states not arise there? … [etc. … 9.2.1.4.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom and in what [state] wholesome states do not arise, for them and in that [state] have unwholesome states not arisen?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, wholesome states do not arise therein;
yet it is not the case that unwholesome states have not arisen therein for them. [This is so] for the inhabitants of the Pure Abodes (*suddhāvāsa*).
When the second consciousness is occurring, for those non-percipient beings, neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states arise there. Or rather:
for whomsoever unwholesome states have not arisen at a certain place, do wholesome states not arise for them there? Yes.
For whom and in what [state] wholesome states do not arise, for them and in that [state] do indeterminate states not arise?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for non-percipient beings— wholesome states do not arise for them in that state, but it is not the case that indeterminate states did not arise for them in that state.
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), neither wholesome states (kusala-dhammā) arise there, nor have indeterminate states (abyākata-dhammā) arisen there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever indeterminate states have not arisen in a certain place, do wholesome states not arise for them there? Yes.
For whom, where unwholesome states do not arise, for them there, indeterminate states did not arise?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and for non-percipient beings—for them, there, unwholesome states do not arise;
yet it is not that for them there indeterminate states did not [arise].
[For those] being reborn in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), neither unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) arise there, nor have indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) arisen there. Or rather:
for whomsoever indeterminate states have not arisen at a certain place, do unwholesome states not arise for them there? Yes.
9.2.1.5. Chapter on the Present and Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra) 9.2.1.5.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) In one for whom wholesome states arise, will unwholesome states also arise?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path,
wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) arise for them, but unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not arise for them.
For others, at the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both wholesome states and [other] states arise for them.
And unwholesome states will arise.
Or again, for whomsoever unwholesome states will arise, do wholesome states arise for them? [The answer is:

No—for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation.
In the case of non-percipient beings, unwholesome states will arise, but wholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both unwholesome states will arise and wholesome states arise for them.
For one in whom wholesome states arise, will indeterminate states arise? Yes.
Or, for whom indeterminate states (abyākata-dhammā) will arise, do wholesome states (kusala-dhammā) arise for them?
For all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation (nirodha-samāpanna) or are non-percipient beings (asañña-satta), indeterminate states will arise, but wholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of arising of wholesome states, indeterminate states will arise for them, and wholesome states are arising.
For whom unwholesome states are arising, will indeterminate states arise for them? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will arise, are unwholesome states arising for them?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will arise, but unwholesome states do not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states arise for them.
9.2.1.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where wholesome states arise, will unwholesome states arise there?
… [as before] … 9.2.1.5.3. Positive Person and Plane (Anuloma-puggala-okāsa)
In whomsoever wholesome states arise at a certain place, will unwholesome states also arise in that person at that same place?
At the moment of the arising of the Supreme Path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the Supreme Path—
in those persons, at that place, wholesome states arise, but unwholesome states do not.
...wholesome states will arise. At the moment of arising of other wholesome states, both wholesome states and unwholesome states will arise for them there.
Or else, for whomsoever unwholesome states will arise in a certain place, do wholesome states arise for them there?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and in those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
unwholesome states will arise there, but wholesome states do not arise there for them.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both unwholesome states and wholesome states will arise there for them.
For whomsoever wholesome states arise at a certain place, will indeterminate states arise for that person at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will arise at a certain place, do wholesome states arise for that person at that same place? [No;
for all beings at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, and for non-percipient beings.
For them, indeterminate states will arise there, but wholesome states do not arise for them there.
At the moment of the arising of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states will arise for them there.
For one in whom unwholesome states are arising at a certain place, will indeterminate states also arise for him there? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will arise at a certain place, do unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) arise for them at that same place?

For all beings at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness (citta-bhaṅga-khaṇa), for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome (akusala-vippayutta-citta),
and for non-percipient beings (asañña-satta)— for these, indeterminate states will arise there, but unwholesome states do not arise for them there.
At the moment of arising of unwholesome states, indeterminate states will arise and unwholesome states are arising for those persons therein.
9.2.1.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not arise, will unwholesome states not arise for them?

In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, in those who have attained cessation, and in non-percipient beings, wholesome states do not arise; yet it is not the case that unwholesome states will not arise for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, in Arahants, and in one whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the supreme path—
At the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness, wholesome states do not arise and unwholesome states will not arise.
Or, conversely, for whom unwholesome states will not arise, do wholesome states not arise at that time?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path, [wholesome states do not arise].
At the moment of arising of consciousness, unwholesome states will not arise for them, but wholesome states do not fail to arise for them.

At the moment of dissolution of the supreme path (aggamagga), in Arahants, and at the moment of dissolution of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path— unwholesome states will not arise for them.
And wholesome states do not arise.
For one in whom wholesome states do not arise, will indeterminate states not arise? [The answer is:
For all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, wholesome states do not arise, yet indeterminate states will not fail to arise for them.
For those possessing their final consciousness, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise, do wholesome states not arise for them? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states do not arise, will indeterminate states not arise for them?

[They will not] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those whose consciousness is dissociated from the unwholesome at the moment of its arising, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, unwholesome states do not arise, yet indeterminate states will not fail to arise for them.
For those possessing their final consciousness, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise.
Or alternatively: For whom indeterminate states will not arise, for that person do unwholesome states not arise?
Yes. 9.2.1.5.5. Negative Plane:
Where wholesome states do not arise, there will unwholesome states not arise? …pe….
9.2.1.5.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, in what [place], wholesome states do not arise, for them, in that [place], unwholesome states will not arise?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those with a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its arising—in these cases, for them, in that [place]...
Wholesome states do not arise, yet it is not the case that unwholesome states will not arise for them there.
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path; at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness immediately preceding the attainment of the supreme path by Arahants;
and for non-percipient beings—at these times, wholesome states do not arise for them there.
Unwholesome states will not arise.
Or, conversely, in whomsoever unwholesome states will not arise at a certain place, do wholesome states not arise in them at that place?

At the moment of the arising of the highest path (agga-magga), and in the case of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the highest path—[in these cases, wholesome states do not arise].

At the moment of arising of consciousness, unwholesome states will not arise for them there, but wholesome states do not fail to arise for them there. At the moment of dissolution of the supreme path;
at the moment of dissolution of that consciousness immediately after which Arahants will attain the supreme path; and for non-percipient beings—[for these]...
In that case, unwholesome states will not arise and wholesome states do not arise.
For whom and where wholesome states do not arise, for them there, will indeterminate states not arise?
[They will not arise] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome, and for non-percipient beings.
For them, wholesome states do not arise there; yet it is not the case that indeterminate states will not arise for them there.
For those possessing the final consciousness, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise there.
Or rather: for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise in a certain place, for that person wholesome states do not arise there? Yes, they do.
For whom and where unwholesome states do not arise, for them and there will unwholesome-resultant (abyākata) states not arise?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome,
and for non-percipient beings— for these, unwholesome states do not arise there, but it is not that unwholesome-resultant states do not arise there for them.
They will arise. For those possessing their final consciousness, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states will arise there.
Or rather: for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise in a certain place, do unwholesome states not arise for them there? Yes.
9.2.1.6. Section on the Past and Future (Atītānāgatavāra) 9.2.1.6.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom wholesome states have arisen, will unwholesome states arise for that person?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for the Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path—
wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) have arisen for them, but unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not arise for them.
For others, both wholesome states have arisen and unwholesome states will arise.
Or again, for whomsoever unwholesome states will arise, for that person have wholesome states arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states have arisen, for that person will indeterminate states arise?

For those possessing their final consciousness, wholesome states have arisen, but indeterminate states will not arise for them. For others, both wholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will arise.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhammā) will arise, for that person have wholesome states (kusala-dhammā) arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states (akusala-dhammā) have arisen, for that person will indeterminate states arise?

For those possessing the final consciousness (pacchima-citta-samaṅgī), unwholesome states have arisen, but indeterminate states will not arise for them. For others, both unwholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will arise.
Or again, for whom indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) will arise, for that person have unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) arisen?
Yes. 9.2.1.6.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where wholesome states have arisen, will unwholesome states arise there? ...pe... (etc.)
9.2.1.6.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what place, unwholesome states will arise, given that wholesome states have arisen?
[They will arise] in those who possess the highest path (agga-magga), in Arahants, and in those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path.
For those [beings], wholesome states have arisen there, but unwholesome states will not arise there for them.
For others— those of the four-constituent and five-constituent realms— both wholesome states have arisen there and unwholesome states will also arise there.
Or again, for whomsoever unwholesome states will arise at a certain place, have wholesome states arisen for them at that same place?
For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), unwholesome states will arise there, but wholesome states have not arisen for them there.
[This is also the case] for others among the four-aggregate and five-aggregate beings.
In those persons, unwholesome states will arise there, and wholesome states have arisen there.
For whomsoever wholesome states have arisen in a certain place, will indeterminate states arise in them there?
In those possessing the final consciousness, wholesome states have arisen there, but indeterminate states will not arise in them there.
Indeterminate states will arise. For those others belonging to the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, both wholesome states and indeterminate states have arisen there.
Or else, for whomsoever indeterminate states will arise at a certain plane, have wholesome states arisen for them there?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, for those non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will arise there,

but wholesome states have not arisen there for them. For others— those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms— both indeterminate states will arise there and wholesome states have arisen there.
For whom and in what [state] unwholesome states have arisen, will indeterminate states arise for them in that same state?
For those possessing the final consciousness, unwholesome states have arisen in that state, but indeterminate states will not arise for them in that state.
For others—those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—[indeterminate states will arise].
Unwholesome states have arisen and indeterminate states will arise.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will arise at a certain place, have unwholesome states arisen for them at that same place?

For those in the second moment of consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states will arise at that place, but unwholesome states have not arisen for them there.

...will arise, but unwholesome states have not arisen for them there. For others—those belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—both indeterminate states will arise and unwholesome states have arisen there.
9.2.1.6.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom wholesome states did not arise, will unwholesome states not arise for them? None.
Or rather, for whom unwholesome states will not arise, did wholesome states not arise for them? They did arise.
For whom wholesome states did not arise, will indeterminate states not arise for them? None.
Or, for whom indeterminate states will not arise, for that person have wholesome states not arisen? They have arisen.
For whom unwholesome states have not arisen, for that person will indeterminate states not arise? There is none.
Or, for whom indeterminate states will not arise, for that person have unwholesome states not arisen? They have arisen.
9.2.1.6.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where wholesome states have not arisen, will unwholesome states not arise there? … [etc.
… 9.2.1.6.6. Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom wholesome states have not arisen at a certain place, will unwholesome states not arise for them at that same place?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Suddhāvāsa deities, wholesome states have not arisen there, yet it is not the case that unwholesome states will not arise for them there. For those non-percipient beings, wholesome states...
And unwholesome states did not arise [for them].
But for whomsoever, wherever, unwholesome states will not arise, for that person there, did wholesome states not arise?
[They did not arise] for those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path.
For them, unwholesome states will not arise there, but wholesome states have not failed to arise there for them.
For non-percipient beings, neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will arise there, and neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states have arisen there for them.
For whomsoever wholesome states (*kusala-dhamma*) have not arisen in a certain place, will indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) not arise for them there? They will arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not arise in a certain place, have wholesome states not arisen for them there? They have arisen.
For whomsoever unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) have not arisen in a certain place, will indeterminate states not arise for them there? They will arise.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will not arise, have unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) arisen there for them? They have arisen.
